hindi: तीन प्रदेष्टा और तीन अमात्य कण्टकशोधन करें।
english: Three pradeṣṭṛs and three ministers should carry out the cleansing of thorns (kaṇṭaka-śodhana).
notes: pradeṣṭṛ kept as a title. kaṇṭaka-śodhana is rendered literally ('cleansing of thorns'); no sense is imported from later usage. 'Three ... three' is read as three of each.
lines_deva: प्रदेष्टारस् त्रयस् त्रयो ऽमात्याः कण्टक.शोधनं कुर्युः

hindi: अर्थ्य-प्रतीकार, कारुओं के शासक, सन्निक्षेप्ता, अपने धन के कारु, श्रेणी को प्रमाण मानने वाले निक्षेप ग्रहण करें।
english: The arthya-pratīkāras, the controllers of artisans, the sannikṣeptṛs, the artisans of their own wealth, [and those] having the guild as authority should take the deposit.
notes: Doubtful words. arthya-pratīkāra is literally 'remedies (pratīkāra) of arthya' (arthya perhaps 'what is needed' or 'petitioners'); kept untranslated. sannikṣeptṛ (sam-ni-√kṣip) is obscure and kept untranslated. sva-vitta-kāru is literally 'artisans of their own wealth'. Whether all five items are subjects of one list or describe one class is not certain.
lines_deva: अर्थ्य.प्रतीकाराः कारु.शासितारः सन्निक्षेप्तारः स्व.वित्त.कारवः श्रेणी.प्रमाणा निक्षेपं गृह्णीयुः
lines_iast: arthya.pratīkārāḥ kāru.śāsitāraḥ sannikṣeptāraḥ sva.vitta.kāravaḥ śreṇī.pramāṇā nikṣepaṃ gṛhṇīyuḥ

hindi: विपत्ति में श्रेणी निक्षेप को अपनाए।
english: In misfortune the guild should take on the deposit.
notes: bhaj is rendered 'take on' (literally 'resort to, share in'); alternatives 'share' or 'make good' are possible.

words.gloss: with place, time and task specified
with place and time not specified

hindi: और जिस कर्म में देश, काल और कार्य निर्दिष्ट हों, वह कर्म करें; जिसमें देश और काल निर्दिष्ट नहीं हैं, उसमें कार्य का अपदेश है।
english: And they should do work whose place, time and task are specified; [for work] whose place and time are not specified, [there is] the designation of the task.
notes: The last phrase is elliptical; apadeśa is rendered 'designation' (alternatives: 'pretext, statement'). The sense of the contrast is uncertain. Review: apadeśam is accusative, so the clause may instead be 'they should do work of unspecified place and time, [giving] a designation of the task'; the copula reading is kept only as the least interpretive. A person should decide.
lines_deva: निर्दिष्ट.देश.काल.कार्यं च कर्म कुर्युः, अनिर्दिष्ट.देश.कालं कार्य.अपदेशम्
lines_iast: nirdiṣṭa.deśa.kāla.kāryaṃ ca karma kuryuḥ, anirdiṣṭa.deśa.kālaṃ kārya.apadeśam

hindi: समय बीत जाने पर वेतन चौथाई कम और उसका दुगुना दण्ड होता है।
english: On exceeding the time, the pay [is] less by a quarter, and the fine [is] twice that.
notes: 'A quarter' of the pay is understood; the Sanskrit says only pāda.
lines_deva: काल.अतिपातने पाद.हीनं वेतनं तद्.द्वि.गुणश् च दण्डः
lines_iast: kāla.atipātane pāda.hīnaṃ vetanaṃ tad.dvi.guṇaś ca daṇḍaḥ

hindi: भ्रेष और उपनिपात को छोड़कर, खोए या नष्ट हुए की भरपाई करें।
english: Except in the case of bhreṣa and upanipāta, they should make good what is lost or destroyed.
notes: bhreṣa is obscure and kept as printed; upanipāta is literally 'falling upon'. abhyāvah is literally 'bring to'; 'make good' is the chosen sense. The dual ablative is read with anyatra.

hindi: कार्य को अन्यथा करने पर वेतन का नाश और उसका दुगुना दण्ड होता है।
english: In doing the work otherwise, [there is] loss of pay and a fine twice that.

hindi: जुलाहे दश-एकादशिक सूत बढ़ाएँ।
english: The weavers should increase the ten-eleven (daśa-ekādaśika) yarn.
notes: daśa-ekādaśika is literally 'of ten and eleven'; its exact sense (a ratio such as eleven for ten?) is not given by the words, so it is kept literal.

hindi: वृद्धि को काटने पर कटे हुए का दुगुना दण्ड होता है।
english: In cutting off the increase, the fine [is] twice the cut.
notes: 'vṛddhic.chede' is the e-text's marking of vṛddhi + chede (cch from c + ch); not a typo. 'Cut' could mean the amount cut off.

hindi: सूत का मूल्य बुनाई का वेतन है; क्षौम और कौशेय का डेढ़ गुना; पत्त्र-ऊर्णा, कम्बल और दुकूल का दुगुना।
english: The price of the yarn [is] the pay for weaving; for linen (kṣauma) and silk (kauśeya), one and a half times; for pattra-ūrṇā, blanket (kambala) and dukūla, twofold.

text_flags.why: single t expected (patra, leaf/cloth); double t may be a typing slip (possible)

notes: The first two phrases may be read either way round (price = pay, or pay = price). pattra-ūrṇā is read as one item and is obscure (literally 'leaf-wool'); dukūla is a cloth name kept as printed. kṣauma = linen and kauśeya = silk are the usual senses (medium confidence).
lines_deva: सूत्र.मूल्यं वान.वेतनं, क्षौम.कौशेयानाम् अध्यर्ध.गुणं, पत्त्र.ऊर्णा.कम्बल.दुकूलानां द्वि.गुणम्
lines_iast: sūtra.mūlyaṃ vāna.vetanaṃ, kṣauma.kauśeyānām adhyardha.guṇaṃ, pattra.ūrṇā.kambala.dukūlānāṃ dvi.guṇam

hindi: माप में कमी होने पर वेतन कमी से घटा हुआ और उसका दुगुना दण्ड होता है; तौल में कमी होने पर कमी का चौगुना दण्ड; सूत बदलने पर मूल्य का दुगुना।
english: In deficient measure, the pay [is] lessened by the shortfall and the fine [is] twice that; in deficient weight, the fine [is] four times the deficiency; in exchanging the yarn, [the fine is] twice the price.
notes: hīna-avahīna is obscure (literally 'deficient-reduced'); rendered 'lessened by the shortfall'. In the last phrase daṇḍa is not repeated in the Sanskrit; supplied in brackets in English only.
lines_deva: मान.हीने हीन.अवहीनं वेतनं तद्.द्वि.गुणश् च दण्डः, तुला.हीने हीन.चतुर्.गुणो दण्डः, सूत्र.परिवर्तने मूल्य.द्वि.गुणः
lines_iast: māna.hīne hīna.avahīnaṃ vetanaṃ tad.dvi.guṇaś ca daṇḍaḥ, tulā.hīne hīna.catur.guṇo daṇḍaḥ, sūtra.parivartane mūlya.dvi.guṇaḥ

hindi: इससे दो पट की बुनाई की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, the weaving of double cloth is explained.
notes: dvi-paṭa is literally 'two cloths'; 'double cloth' is the natural rendering.

hindi: ऊन की तुला के लिए पाँच पल का विहनन-छेद और रोम-छेद है।
english: For a tulā of wool, [there is] a five-pala beating-cut (vihanana-cheda) and a cut of hair (roma-cheda).
notes: Obscure. vihanana is literally 'beating, striking'; cheda 'cut, cutting off'. Whether 'five palas' belongs to both cuts or only the first is not clear. The genitive 'of the wool-tulā' is rendered 'for'.

words.gloss: on wooden boards and smooth stones

hindi: धोबी काठ के तख्तों और चिकनी शिलाओं पर कपड़े धोएँ।
english: Washermen should wash cloths on wooden boards and smooth stones.
notes: rajaka could also mean dyer; 'washer' fits nenijyuḥ.

hindi: अन्यत्र धोने वाले वस्त्र की हानि और छह पण का दण्ड दें।
english: Those washing elsewhere should give [for] the damage to the cloth and a fine of six paṇas.
notes: Literally 'should give the damage to the cloth'; the sense is compensation, but the Sanskrit does not say so. nenijataḥ is read as nominative plural.
lines_deva: अन्यत्र नेनिजतो वस्त्र.उपघातं षट्.पणं च दण्डं दद्युः
lines_iast: anyatra nenijato vastra.upaghātaṃ ṣaṭ.paṇaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ dadyuḥ

words.gram: pres. part. mid. nom. pl. pari-√dhā

hindi: मुद्गर के चिह्न से अन्य वस्त्र पहनने वाले तीन पण का दण्ड दें।
english: Those wearing cloth other than [that with] the mallet mark should give a fine of three paṇas.
notes: mudgara-aṅka is literally 'mark of the mallet'.
lines_deva: मुद्गर.अङ्काद् अन्यद् वासः परिदधानास् त्रि.पणं दण्डं दद्युः
lines_iast: mudgara.aṅkād anyad vāsaḥ paridadhānās tri.paṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyuḥ

words.gloss: in sale, hire and pledge of another's cloth
words.gram: tat-puruṣa with dvandva, n. loc. pl.

hindi: दूसरे के वस्त्र की बिक्री, किराये और बन्धक में बारह पण का दण्ड है; अदला-बदली में मूल्य का दुगुना और वस्त्र का दान।
english: In sale, hire and pledge of another's cloth, the fine [is] twelve paṇas; in exchange, [the fine is] twice the price, and the giving of cloth.
notes: avakraya is rendered 'hire' (alternative: 'purchase'); ādhāna 'pledge'. 'The giving of cloth' is literal; it may mean restitution of cloth, but the Sanskrit does not say so. 'Another's' (para) is read with vastra. Review: avakraya = hire is kept, aligned with 5.2 avakrītaka = hired; the alternative is 'purchase'.
lines_deva: पर.वस्त्र.विक्रय.अवक्रय.आधानेषु च द्वादश.पणो दण्डः, परिवर्तने मूल्य.द्वि.गुणो वस्त्र.दानं च
lines_iast: para.vastra.vikraya.avakraya.ādhāneṣu ca dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, parivartane mūlya.dvi.guṇo vastra.dānaṃ ca

words.gloss: of the colour of washed yarn

hindi: मुकुल-अवदात, शिलापट्ट पर शुद्ध, धुले सूत के रंग वाला और पोंछकर श्वेत किया हुआ वस्त्र एक रात बाद दें।
english: They should give [them] — mukula-avadāta, clean on a stone slab, of the colour of washed yarn, and wiped white — one night later.
notes: mukula-avadāta is literally 'bud-white' (or 'bud-clean'); kept as printed with the literal sense here. Hindi adds the noun वस्त्र for the neuter adjectives. eka-rātra-uttara is literally 'one night later' (alternative: 'more than one night').
lines_deva: मुकुल.अवदातं शिला.पट्ट.शुद्धं धौत.सूत्र.वर्णं प्रमृष्ट.श्वेतं च-एक.रात्र.उत्तरं दद्युः
lines_iast: mukula.avadātaṃ śilā.paṭṭa.śuddhaṃ dhauta.sūtra.varṇaṃ pramṛṣṭa.śvetaṃ ca-eka.rātra.uttaraṃ dadyuḥ

words.gloss: dyed with flowers, lac and mañjiṣṭhā

hindi: पाँच रात का हल्के रंग वाला; छह रात का नीला; फूल, लाख और मञ्जिष्ठा से रँगा, भारी परिकर्म वाला, यत्न से उपचार करने योग्य, उत्तम जाति का वस्त्र सात रात का।
english: The five-night, lightly dyed; the six-night, blue; and the seven-night cloth — dyed with flowers, lac and mañjiṣṭhā, of heavy treatment, to be treated with care, of fine kind.
notes: No verb is stated; the list probably continues the 'dadyuḥ' of the previous unit but this is not in the text. '-rātrika' is rendered literally 'of N nights'. mañjiṣṭhā is a dye-stuff name kept as printed. jātya is rendered 'of fine kind' (alternative: 'genuine').
lines_deva: पञ्च.रात्रिकं तनु.रागं, षड्.रात्रिकं नीलं, पुष्प.लाक्षा.मञ्जिष्ठा.रक्तं गुरु.परिकर्म यत्न.उपचार्यं जात्यं वासः सप्त.रात्रिकम्
lines_iast: pañca.rātrikaṃ tanu.rāgaṃ, ṣaḍ.rātrikaṃ nīlaṃ, puṣpa.lākṣā.mañjiṣṭhā.raktaṃ guru.parikarma yatna.upacāryaṃ jātyaṃ vāsaḥ sapta.rātrikam

hindi: उसके बाद वे वेतन की हानि प्राप्त करें।
english: After that, they should incur loss of pay.

hindi: रंगाई के विवादों में विश्वसनीय कुशल लोग वेतन निर्धारित करें।
english: In disputes about dyeing, trustworthy experts should fix the pay.
notes: rāga is read as 'dye, colour' (dyeing).

hindi: सबसे मूल्यवान् के लिए एक पण वेतन है; मध्यम के लिए आधा पण; सबसे निम्न के लिए चौथाई; मोटे के लिए माषक, दो माषक; रँगे हुए के लिए दुगुना।
english: For the most valuable, the pay [is] a paṇa; for the middling, half a paṇa; for the lowest, a quarter; for the coarse, a māṣaka, two māṣakas; for the dyed, twofold.
notes: The nouns qualified (the cloths) are not stated. 'A quarter' is of a paṇa by implication. māṣaka-dvi-māṣaka may mean 'one or two māṣakas'; kept literal. raktaka/sthūlaka may be cloth-class names.
lines_deva: परार्ध्यानां पणो वेतनं, मध्यमानाम् अर्ध.पणः, प्रत्यवराणां पादः, स्थूलकानां माषक.द्वि.माषकं, द्वि.गुणं रक्तकानाम्
lines_iast: parārdhyānāṃ paṇo vetanaṃ, madhyamānām ardha.paṇaḥ, pratyavarāṇāṃ pādaḥ, sthūlakānāṃ māṣaka.dvi.māṣakaṃ, dvi.guṇaṃ raktakānām

hindi: पहली धुलाई में चौथा भाग क्षय है, दूसरी में पाँचवाँ भाग।
english: In the first washing, the loss [is] a fourth part; in the second, a fifth part.

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: uttara is read as 'what follows' (the later washings); alternative 'the higher/latter'.

hindi: धोबियों के द्वारा दर्ज़ियों की व्याख्या की गई है।
english: The tailors are explained by the washermen.
notes: The instrumental is kept literal; the meaning is probably that the rules just given for washermen apply to tailors, but the Sanskrit does not say so. tunna-vāya 'tailor' (literally 'sewn-weaver') is the usual sense.

hindi: सुनारों में जो अशुद्ध हाथ से चाँदी, सोना बिना बताए खरीदते हैं, उनके लिए समान रूप वाले पर बारह पण का दण्ड, बदले रूप वाले पर चौबीस पण, चोर के हाथ से अड़तालीस पण।
english: Of goldsmiths who buy silver [or] gold from an impure hand without declaring [it]: [if it is] of the same form, the fine [is] twelve paṇas; [if] of altered form, twenty-four paṇas; [if bought] from a thief's hand, forty-eight paṇas.

text_flags.why: possible: the compound marker '.' is missing here, unlike dvādaśa.paṇo in unit 17 and 28

notes: The genitive 'of goldsmiths' is rendered 'of goldsmiths who buy', following krīṇatām. aśuci-hasta (literally 'impure hand') is kept literal. sarūpa / virūpa are rendered 'of the same form' / 'of altered form' (the exact sense is not given). rūpya is read as silver. Review: the flag on dvādaśapaṇo is confirmed (missing dot). suvarṇa here is the metal, gold; in 4.1.28 and 4.1.32 it is the unit.
lines_deva: सुवर्ण.काराणाम् अशुचि.हस्ताद् रूप्यं सुवर्णम् अनाख्याय सरूपं क्रीणतां द्वादशपणो दण्डः, विरूपं चतुर्.विंशति.पणः, चोर.हस्ताद् अष्ट.चत्वारिंशत्.पणः
lines_iast: suvarṇa.kārāṇām aśuci.hastād rūpyaṃ suvarṇam anākhyāya sarūpaṃ krīṇatāṃ dvādaśapaṇo daṇḍaḥ, virūpaṃ catur.viṃśati.paṇaḥ, cora.hastād aṣṭa.catvāriṃśat.paṇaḥ

words.gloss: in purchases concealed, of altered form, or below the price

hindi: छिपे हुए, बदले रूप वाले और मूल्य से हीन क्रयों में चोरी का दण्ड है, और बने हुए भाण्ड में छल पर भी।
english: In purchases [that are] concealed, of altered form, [or] short of the price, the fine for theft [applies]; and in deceit about made wares.
notes: The compound is read as pracchanna / virūpa / mūlya-hīna-kraya (three kinds of purchase). upadhi is rendered 'deceit'; kṛta-bhāṇḍa is literally 'made ware'.

hindi: सुवर्ण में से एक माषक ले जाने वाले को दो सौ का दण्ड; चाँदी के धरण में से एक माषक ले जाने वाले को बारह पण।
english: For one who takes away a māṣaka from a suvarṇa, the fine [is] two hundred; for one who takes away a māṣaka from a silver dharaṇa, twelve paṇas.
notes: suvarṇa is both 'gold' and a unit of weight; the weight sense is chosen but the first reading 'from gold' is possible. The unit of 'two hundred' is not stated (paṇas by implication). dharaṇa kept as a unit name. Suvarṇān is suvarṇāt before m. Review: suvarṇa is read as the weight unit because it stands parallel to rūpya-dharaṇāt; suvarṇa, dharaṇa and māṣaka stay unit names.
lines_deva: सुवर्णान् माषकम् अपहरतो द्वि.शतो दण्डः, रूप्य.धरणान् माषकम् अपहरतो द्वादश.पणः
lines_iast: suvarṇān māṣakam apaharato dvi.śato daṇḍaḥ, rūpya.dharaṇān māṣakam apaharato dvādaśa.paṇaḥ

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: Same wording as unit 24.

hindi: वर्ण का उत्कर्ष, अपसारण या योग सिद्ध करने वाले को पाँच सौ का दण्ड।
english: For one who effects raising of colour, removal, or a combination, the fine [is] five hundred.
notes: varṇa is read as 'colour' (alternatives 'quality, class'); yoga as 'combination' (see the doubt about yoga in the glossary). Unit of 'five hundred' is not stated.
lines_deva: वर्ण.उत्कर्षम् अपसारणं योगं वा साधयतः पञ्च.शतो दण्डः
lines_iast: varṇa.utkarṣam apasāraṇaṃ yogaṃ vā sādhayataḥ pañca.śato daṇḍaḥ

hindi: उन दोनों के अपचरण में रंग का अपहार जाने।
english: In the misconduct of those two, he should know [it as] the taking away of the colour.
notes: 'Those two' probably refers to the two things just named (utkarṣa, apasāraṇa, yoga) but this is not clear. apacaraṇa is literally 'going wrong'. rāga 'colour' here may mean dye or colour of the metal.

hindi: चाँदी के धरण के लिए वेतन एक माषक है, सुवर्ण के लिए आठवाँ भाग।
english: The pay [is] a māṣaka for a silver dharaṇa, [and] an eighth part for a suvarṇa.
notes: 'An eighth part' of what is not stated (of a māṣaka by implication).

hindi: विशेष शिक्षा से वेतन की वृद्धि दुगुनी है।
english: By special training, the increase of pay [is] twofold.

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: uttara could be 'the following (rule/case)' or 'the rest'. The same formula recurs in units 34, 38, 43, 47.

words.gloss: copper, vṛtta, bell-metal, vaikṛntaka, āra, kūṭaka

hindi: ताम्र, वृत्त, कंस, वैकृन्तक, आर और कूटक का वेतन सौ में पाँच है।
english: Of copper, vṛtta, bell-metal, vaikṛntaka, āra and kūṭaka, the pay is five in the hundred.
notes: vṛtta, vaikṛntaka, āra and kūṭaka are metal/alloy names left untranslated; kaṃsa = bell-metal. 'pañcakaṃ śatam' read as five per hundred; the unit of the wage is not stated. The genitive plural may govern 'articles/work of' these metals (not supplied).

hindi: ताँबे के पिण्ड में दसवें भाग का क्षय है।
english: A lump of copper [has] a loss of a tenth part.
notes: daśa-bhāga read as 'a tenth part'; 'ten parts' is the literal alternative. kṣaya = loss/wastage (in working the metal). The copula is supplied.

hindi: पल में कमी होने पर कमी का दुगुना दण्ड है।
english: When [it is] deficient in palas, the fine is twice the deficiency.
notes: pala-hīne is read as a locative 'on a shortfall in pala (weight)'; the thing weighed is not stated. hīna-dvi-guṇa read as 'twice the deficiency'.

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: uttara could be 'the following (rule/case)' or 'the rest'. The same formula recurs in units 34, 38, 43, 47.

hindi: सीसे और रांगे के पिण्ड में बीसवें भाग का क्षय है।
english: A lump of lead and tin [has] a loss of a twentieth part.
notes: sīsa = lead, trapu = tin (glossary). 'Lump of lead and tin' could mean each separately or an alloy; viṃśati-bhāga read as 'a twentieth part'. Copula supplied.

hindi: और इसके पल का वेतन काकणी है।
english: And a kākaṇī is the pay for a pala of this.
notes: asya refers back to the metal of the preceding unit (lead and tin). pala-vetanam read as 'pay per pala'. kākaṇī left as the coin/measure name.

hindi: काले लोहे के पिण्ड में पाँचवें भाग का क्षय है।
english: A lump of black iron [has] a loss of a fifth part.
notes: kāla-āyasa read literally 'black iron'. pañca-bhāga read as 'a fifth part' (literal alternative: five parts). Copula supplied.

hindi: और इसके पल का वेतन दो काकणी है।
english: And two kākaṇīs are the pay for a pala of this.
notes: asya refers to the iron of the preceding unit.

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: uttara could be 'the following (rule/case)' or 'the rest'. The same formula recurs in units 34, 38, 43, 47.

words.gram: pres. part. m. gen. sg. caus. √kup
pres. part. m. gen. sg. caus. √kup

hindi: सिक्का-परीक्षक का — जो स्थित पण-यात्रा को, जो विचलित करने योग्य नहीं है, विचलित करता है, विचलित करने योग्य को विचलित नहीं करता — उसके लिए बारह पण का दण्ड है।
english: For the coin-examiner who disturbs the established paṇa-yātrā that is not to be disturbed, [or] does not disturb one that is to be disturbed, the fine is twelve paṇas.
notes: Obscure: paṇa-yātrā kept as a term (possibly the course/circulation of paṇas, i.e. the currency; or a fee). kopayati (caus. of √kup, 'make angry/disturb') is rendered literally; commonly understood as 'reject/treat as spoiled' but that sense is not asserted. rūpa = coin (glossary 5.2). 'or' in English brackets is supplied (asyndeton).
lines_deva: रूप.दर्शकस्य स्थितां पण.यात्राम् अकोप्यां कोपयतः कोप्याम् अकोपयतो द्वादश.पणो दण्डः
lines_iast: rūpa.darśakasya sthitāṃ paṇa.yātrām akopyāṃ kopayataḥ kopyām akopayato dvādaśa.paṇo daṇḍaḥ

words.gloss: in the clearing of the vyājī

hindi: व्याजी की परिशुद्धि होने पर पण-यात्रा।
english: On the clearing of the vyājī, [it is] the paṇa-yātrā.
notes: Obscure: vyājī left untranslated (a charge/premium or allowance); pariśuddhi = clearing/settling/purification. No predicate in the text; the copula in English brackets is supplied. Sense low confidence. Hindi व्याजी is kept as a term and is not Hindi व्याज 'interest'; no sense is asserted.

words.gram: pres. part. m. gen. sg. upa-√jīv

hindi: जो पणों में माषक पर जीविका चलाता है, उसके लिए बारह पण का दण्ड है।
english: For one who lives on a māṣaka [out of] the paṇas, the fine is twelve paṇas.
notes: Both paṇān and māṣakam are accusative with upajīvataḥ; the text is elliptical. Read as 'living on (taking) a māṣaka from the paṇas'; alternative: 'living on paṇas and a māṣaka'. The bracketed 'out of' and the Hindi 'में' are supplied.

hindi: इससे आगे वाले की व्याख्या की गई।
english: By that, what follows is explained.
notes: uttara could be 'the following (rule/case)' or 'the rest'. The same formula recurs in units 34, 38, 43, 47.

words.gram: pres. part. m. gen. sg. caus. √kṛ
pres. part. m. gen. sg. prati-√grah
pres. part. m. gen. sg. caus. nir-√yā
pres. part. m. gen. sg. pra-√kṣip

hindi: खोटा सिक्का बनवाने वाले, लेने वाले या बाहर भेजने वाले के लिए एक हज़ार का दण्ड है; कोश में डालने वाले के लिए वध है।
english: For one who has a false coin made, accepts it, or sends it out, the fine is a thousand; for one who throws it into the treasury, death.
notes: kūṭa-rūpa = false coin (glossary 5.2). niryāpayati (caus. nir-√yā, 'cause to go out') is rendered literally 'sends out' (possibly 'passes off/puts into circulation'). The unit of the thousand is not stated. 'it' is supplied in English as object of the later participles.
lines_deva: कूट.रूपं कारयतः प्रतिगृह्णतो निर्यापयतो वा सहस्रं दण्डः, कोशे प्रक्षिपतो वधः
lines_iast: kūṭa.rūpaṃ kārayataḥ pratigṛhṇato niryāpayato vā sahasraṃ daṇḍaḥ, kośe prakṣipato vadhaḥ

words.gloss: a third part of the valuables

hindi: चरक और धूल धोने वाले — बहुमूल्य वस्तुओं का तिहाई भाग; राजा — दो; और रत्न।
english: Wanderers and dust-washers: a third part of the valuables; the king: two [parts], and the gem.
notes: Obscure and elliptical; no verb in the text. caraka read literally 'wanderer' (alternatives: a class of prospectors, or spies); pāṃsu-dhāvaka = dust-washer. sāra = valuables per glossary (alternatively the best part of the yield). 'parts' is supplied in English brackets; whether the king takes the two remaining parts and the gem is the likely reading, not stated. The commas separate: first part for the finders, second for the king.
lines_deva: चरक.पांसु.धावकाः सार.त्रि.भागं, द्वौ राजा रत्नं च
lines_iast: caraka.pāṃsu.dhāvakāḥ sāra.tri.bhāgaṃ, dvau rājā ratnaṃ ca

hindi: रत्न के अपहरण पर सर्वोच्च दण्ड है।
english: For theft of a gem, the highest fine.
notes: The text gives no verb; 'for' and the Hindi 'पर' show the relation. uttama = highest (of a graded series of fines, here unspecified). The final visarga of apahāraḥ is dropped in the e-text before a vowel by regular sandhi.

words.gloss: in reports of mines, gems and treasure-troves

hindi: खान, रत्न और निधि की सूचना देने के विषय में सूचना देने वाला छठा अंश पाए, भृतक बारहवाँ अंश।
english: In reporting mines, gems and treasure-troves, the informant should get a sixth share, the hired man a twelfth share.
notes: nivettā read as the one who reports (ni-√vid, 'inform'); nivedana = reporting. The second 'labheta' is understood in both languages. bhṛtaka = hired man (the hired man of the finder or the one employed, not specified).
lines_deva: खनि.रत्न.निधि.निवेदनेषु षष्ठम् अंशं निवेत्ता लभेत, द्वादशम् अंशं भृतकः
lines_iast: khani.ratna.nidhi.nivedaneṣu ṣaṣṭham aṃśaṃ nivettā labheta, dvādaśam aṃśaṃ bhṛtakaḥ

hindi: एक लाख से ऊपर की निधि राजा को जाने वाली है।
english: A treasure-trove above a hundred thousand goes to the king.
notes: śata-sahasra = a hundred thousand (Hindi एक लाख); the unit of value is not stated. 'of [value]' is not supplied; 'above a hundred thousand' is read as the value of the nidhi.

hindi: कम होने पर छठा अंश दे।
english: If [it is] less, he should give a sixth share.
notes: Giver and recipient are not stated (probably the finder giving to the king, cf. unit 52 and 54). ūne = in the lesser case (a nidhi below a hundred thousand).

words.gloss: by his own means of proof

hindi: पूर्व पीढ़ियों की निधि को शुद्ध जानपद अपने प्रमाण से पूरा पाए।
english: A pure country person should get in full a treasure-trove of former generations, by his own means of proof.
notes: paurva-pauruṣika read as 'of former generations' (ancestral). śuci = pure (alternative: honest). karaṇa read as 'means of proof / document' (alternative: 'instrument, act'). jānapada = country person (glossary: country people).
lines_deva: पौर्वपौरुषिकं निधिं जानपदः शुचिः स्व.करणेन समग्रं लभेत
lines_iast: paurvapauruṣikaṃ nidhiṃ jānapadaḥ śuciḥ sva.karaṇena samagraṃ labheta

words.gloss: in the absence of his own means of proof

hindi: अपने प्रमाण के अभाव में पाँच सौ का दण्ड है; छिपाकर लेने पर हज़ार।
english: In the absence of his own means of proof, the fine is five hundred; in secret taking, a thousand.
notes: '[the fine is]' is understood for the second clause. The unit of the fine is not stated. karaṇa as in unit 54.

words.gram: pres. part. m. gen. sg. upa-√kram

words.gloss: by a fault in the action

hindi: जो वैद्य प्राणों के लिए बाधक को बिना बताए उपक्रम करे, उसके विपत्ति होने पर प्रथम साहस-दण्ड है; कर्म के अपराध से विपत्ति होने पर मध्यम।
english: For a physician who undertakes [a case] endangering life without informing [anyone], in a mishap the first fine for rashness; in a mishap through a fault in the action, the middle one.
notes: prāṇa-ābādhika (acc. n.) has no stated noun: 'a case' is supplied in English brackets (the object of upakram, 'undertake/begin treatment'). vipatti = mishap/failure, not specified (death, harm). karma = action (glossary); likely the treatment itself. 'first' and 'middle' refer to the graded sāhasa fines (pūrva-, madhyama-sāhasa); '[anyone]' is supplied. The second 'daṇḍaḥ' is understood.
lines_deva: भिषजः प्राण.आबाधिकम् अनाख्याय-उपक्रममाणस्य विपत्तौ पूर्वः साहस.दण्डः, कर्म.अपराधेन विपत्तौ मध्यमः
lines_iast: bhiṣajaḥ prāṇa.ābādhikam anākhyāya-upakramamāṇasya vipattau pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, karma.aparādhena vipattau madhyamaḥ

words.gloss: in causing injury to a vital spot, death or impairment

hindi: मर्म पर चोट, वध या विकलता करने पर दण्ड-पारुष्य जाने।
english: In causing injury to a vital spot, death or impairment, one should know [it] as physical injury (daṇḍa-pāruṣya).
notes: daṇḍa-pāruṣya = physical injury per glossary (Book 3 sense, the offence-class of assault; literally 'harshness of force'), not 'harshness of punishment' of 8.3. marma-vadha could be read 'killing at a vital spot' instead of three separate items. Hindi keeps the term दण्ड-पारुष्य because the sense is the offence-class. '[it]' supplied. Consistency: vadha is 'death' in unit 48; here marma-vadha is rendered 'injury to a vital spot'. A person should decide between the three-item and the 'killing/striking at a vital spot' readings.

hindi: कुशीलव वर्षाकाल में एक स्थान पर स्थित होकर निवास करें।
english: The kuśīlavas should dwell, staying in one place, during the rainy season.
notes: kuśīlava kept as a term (glossary). varṣā-rātra read as 'rainy season' (accusative of duration).

hindi: अत्यधिक इच्छा-दान और एक का अधिक बोलना छोड़ें।
english: They should avoid excessive giving at will and the over-speaking of one.
notes: Obscure: kāma-dāna read literally 'giving of/at will'; ativāda = over-speaking (alternatives: excessive praise or abuse; 'of one' may mean of a single person or of a single performer). Rendered literally without commitment. atimātram is taken with kāma-dānam only (or both).

hindi: उसका अतिक्रमण होने पर बारह पण का दण्ड है।
english: In transgression of that, the fine is twelve paṇas.

words.gloss: by ridicule of region, caste, gotra, caraṇa and sexual intercourse

hindi: चाहें तो देश, जाति, गोत्र, चरण और मैथुन के उपहास से हँसी-मज़ाक करें।
english: As they like, they may jest by ridiculing region, caste, gotra, caraṇa and sexual intercourse.
notes: kāmam = 'as one likes, certainly'. caraṇa left untranslated (Vedic school or conduct). avahāsa = ridicule/derision. The jest is read as ridicule of those subjects; alternative: jest by mimicry.

hindi: कुशीलवों के द्वारा चारण और भिक्षुक समझाए गए हैं।
english: By [what is said of] the kuśīlavas, the cāraṇas and mendicants are explained.
notes: The instrumental means that the rules for the kuśīlavas also explain (apply to) the cāraṇas and mendicants, as in the formula 'tena uttaraṃ vyākhyātam'. The bracketed phrase is supplied. cāraṇa kept as a term (wandering bards).

hindi: उनके लिए लोहे के शूल से जितने पण वे कहें, उतने शिफा के प्रहार दण्ड हैं।
english: For them, as many paṇas as they declare by an iron spike, so many strokes of the śiphā are the fines.
notes: Obscure: abhi-√vad rendered 'declare' (possibly 'demand/claim'); 'by an iron spike' is taken with the declaring (alternative: the spike marks or is the means of the claim); śiphā = lash/thong (a root-fibre whip), kept as śiphā. 'For them' fits teṣām (gen. pl.) loosely.
lines_deva: तेषाम् अयः.शूलेन यावतः पणान् अभिवदेयुस् तावन्तः शिफा.प्रहारा दण्डाः
lines_iast: teṣām ayaḥ.śūlena yāvataḥ paṇān abhivadeyus tāvantaḥ śiphā.prahārā daṇḍāḥ

hindi: शेष कर्मों का, शिल्पियों का निष्पत्ति-वेतन निर्धारित करे।
english: Of the remaining works, he should fix the craftsmen's completion-pay.
notes: karma = work (glossary 5.3, works of craftsmen). niṣpatti-vetana read as pay on completion (alternative: pay according to outcome). The subject (the superintendent or king) is not stated.

hindi: इस प्रकार चोरों को, अचोर नाम वाले वणिक, कारु, कुशीलव, भिक्षुक, कुहक और दूसरों को देश-पीड़न से रोके।
english: In this way he should restrain thieves, [and] those called non-thieves, merchants, artisans, kuśīlavas, mendicants, kuhakas and others, from affliction of the country.
notes: The verse (anuṣṭubh) is read as: thieves, and those who have the name of non-thieves (merchants, artisans, kuśīlavas, mendicants, tricksters and others). 'and' in brackets is supplied. deśa-pīḍanāt literally 'from affliction of the country' (i.e. from afflicting it). kuhaka kept as 'trickster' (alternative: juggler, deceiver). 'Others' follows ca-anyān. kuhaka kept as a term (kuhakas, कुहक); 'trickster' is a possible sense only.
